turn_text: Senator, until you introduced legislation, I wasn't aware that you could go to the meat case and buy a product that had a label that said product of the USA that wasn't from the USA.

That's right. And isn't that about as close to false advertising as you're ever going to get? Here's what we found. You can have product of the USA on a meat product where the livestock come from out of the country, they're brought into the country as perhaps hanging carcasses or boxed beef. And when it comes in, as long as it is processed again in the United States, it gets to have that label. And I think that's false advertising. So what Senator Thune and I have proposed is that if you want to use that label, and this is a voluntary program to use a label, you know, product of the USA, If you want to use that label, it's born, raised, and processed in the United States. That way folks that are here that want to buy US beef, if they're in South Dakota and they'd rather have some of that high quality stuff that we do in the upper Midwest, then they ought to be able to look at that and say that's a USA product and it's got a label on it and I can trust it. But the last thing in the world they want to do is try to support their local producers, buy a product that says, you know, product of the USA and then find out that was really the product of the USA was the fact that Since it was shipped into the United States, unboxed and reboxed, it could have come from any other part of the world. And I like what we do here to provide high quality beef, and I think we ought to be promoting it. And I don't think there's any problem with the World Trade Organization, the WTO, which causes all the problem with the country of origin labeling that we've tried to do in the past. This is a voluntary program, and we think this meets the standards that WTO would offer because Canada does it already.
